- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≥0.4) and prices are falling, model underestimates drop; add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong negative trend (e.g., 1.0 or 0.67) and true outcome drops sharply, model fails to capture depth; apply 1–3% downward bias for 10–15 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if forecast is rising >0.5% per day for 3+ days, check for sentiment reversal; if sentiment turns negative, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.4% per day.
- For sentiment history with 0.00–0.20, model often underestimates volatility; add 0.3–0.7% upward adjustment to forecast for next 3–5 days.
